stem:
Lalit draws two straight lines that meet at a point. One of the angles at the meeting point measures 70°. He needs the adjacent angle that sits on the same straight line with that 70° angle.

Which measure is correct?

options.text: 70°, because adjacent angles on that straight line must be equal.
110°, because a linear pair on a straight line adds to 180°, so 180° − 70° = 110°.

teacher.key_rationale: A linear pair of adjacent angles on a straight line sums to 180°, so the neighbour is 110°. Claiming the angles must be equal reverses the supplementary relation. Doubling 70° omits the 180° condition. Using 90° − 70° brings in a right-angle rule outside this hinge.

mx_swap.reason: A bare rename of 'linear pair' is weaker than equal-angle reversal, doubling without 180°, and right-angle scope error; kept those three.
